How to use this calculator

  1. Enter your annual income, partner or spouse income, assumed combined effective tax rate.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How marriage tax is calculated

This combines the two annual amounts and applies one assumed effective rate. It does not model filing status, tax brackets, credits or separate state and local taxes. Formula: Combined estimate = (income 1 + income 2) × (1 − assumed effective rate). Use the displayed details to inspect the intermediate amounts and replace example assumptions with terms from your own quote or records.

Combined estimate = (income 1 + income 2) × (1 − assumed effective rate).
A worked example

Combining $80,000 and $60,000 at an assumed 22% effective rate yields an illustrative $109,200 after tax.

Assumptions & useful context

The two-person estimate uses one assumed effective rate and does not model filing-status rules.

Financial projections use your assumptions. Actual returns, lender terms, fees and tax rules can differ; these results do not guarantee a future outcome.

Frequently asked questions

Marriage Tax Calculator: what does the result include?

No. It applies one assumed effective rate to combined income and is only a broad scenario. Filing status and tax brackets can change the result.

Marriage Tax Calculator: which assumptions matter most?

Use the same effective-rate assumption consistently for a rough comparison, then model credits, deductions and local taxes separately.
